title: Pind Daan Samagri List — Complete Materials Required for Gaya Shradh Ceremony
metaDescription: Complete list of Pind Daan samagri (ritual materials) required for Gaya Shradh — rice, sesame, barley, flowers, kusha grass, sacred thread, and what Pitraya Rituals provides in every package.
author: Acharya Pandit V. K. Gayawal

summary: A complete Pind Daan ceremony requires specific ritual materials (samagri) listed in the Dharmashastra. This guide details every required ingredient, its spiritual significance, and how Pitraya Rituals provides everything in every package.
content:
The Pind Daan samagri (ritual materials) are precisely enumerated in the Grihyasutras and Dharmashastra texts. No ceremony is spiritually valid without all required materials being present and ritually purified before the ceremony begins.

### Primary Samagri (Mandatory)

**1. Cooked Rice (Pakwanna / Charu)**
Freshly cooked, plain white rice without salt — the primary matter of the Pinda. Must be cooked on the day of the ceremony.

**2. Black Sesame Seeds (Krishna Tila)**
The single most important ingredient. The Garuda Purana states that sesame seeds were created from Lord Vishnu's sweat and carry supreme purifying power. No Pinda is ritually valid without sesame.

**3. Barley Flour (Yava Atta)**
Mixed with cooked rice to give the Pinda its firm shape. Barley represents abundance and family lineage continuity.

**4. Cow's Milk (Gau Dugdha)**
Used for moistening and binding the Pinda. Must be fresh, unpackaged milk from a cow.

**5. Honey (Madhu)**
Added to the Pinda mixture as a sacred sweetener representing the sweetness of liberation.

**6. Cow's Ghee (Gau Ghrita)**
Poured over the Pindas as an offering. Ghee connects the offering to the divine realm.

**7. Kusha Grass (Darbha Grass)**
Sacred grass used for purifying the ritual space and as a seat (asana) for the Gayawal Purohit.

**8. Ganga Jal (Gangaa Water)**
Used for Tarpan (water libations). Pitraya Rituals provides pure Ganga water sourced from Patna Ghat.

**9. Sacred Thread (Janoi / Yajnopavita)**
Worn by the performer during the ceremony as a mark of ritual purity.

**10. Banana Leaves**
Used as plates on which the Pindas are placed during the offering.

**11. Flowers (Flowers of the Season)**
Fresh flowers offered to the ancestor deity — white flowers preferred.

**12. Incense and Camphor (Dhoop and Kapoor)**
For creating the sacred ritual atmosphere and invoking divine presence.

sections.heading: Samagri NOT Allowed in Pind Daan
sections.body: The following are strictly prohibited in the Pind Daan ceremony: salt (lavan), non-vegetarian items of any kind, processed or packaged foods, plastic containers, and red flowers. The ceremony space must be free of shoes, leather items, and electronic devices.

faqs.question: Can I bring my own samagri from home to Gaya?
faqs.answer: You can bring personal items like your ancestor's photograph and gotra details. However, ritual samagri (sesame, rice, flowers) should be freshly sourced in Gaya on the day of the ceremony as per Dharmashastra requirements. Pitraya provides all samagri as part of our packages.

faqs.question: Why are black sesame seeds (kala til) so important in Pind Daan?
faqs.answer: According to the Garuda Purana, Lord Vishnu created sesame seeds from his divine body — they carry a unique purifying frequency. The Dharmasindhu declares: 'Without sesame, no Shradh ceremony has any validity.' They are the single non-negotiable ingredient.
